capability_assessments.rationale: A receding-horizon MPC searches therapies using the identified CTMC and its cost is compared with observed courses in simulation, which meets L4 in the narrow in-model sense. Evidence is 10 sampled patients drawn from the fitting cohort and scored under the same model, with no held-out predictive validation, so the demonstrated level is limited to feasibility.

Standalone model:B097:uc-ctmc:v1 implements persistent state, continuous-time Markov dynamics, and EM-identified mode-specific transition rate matrices (24 matrices from 3,318 patients), but reports NO held-out predictive transition evaluation (rollout.one_step_evaluated is not_reported) and no representation-quality evaluation. Standalone dynamics capability is therefore honestly recorded as unknown, while the composed controller system:B097:ctmc-mpc:v1 demonstrates narrow in-model L4 feasibility on 10 sampled patients from the fitting cohort.

legacy_cells.B: Data-Driven Modeling and Predictive Control of Chronic Diseases: An Ulcerative Colitis Application
legacy_cells.C: Kopp, Fionna B., Schalkamp, Ann-Kathrin, Azzam, Shadera, Rudrapatna, Vivek, Borrelli, Francesco
legacy_cells.S: Does a receding-horizon therapy policy produce simulated ulcerative-colitis outcomes comparable to the observed clinical course?
legacy_cells.T: Adults with ulcerative colitis in a single-center EHR cohort; the identified model used trajectories from 3,318 patients.
legacy_cells.V: Select a maintenance therapy regimen at a gastroenterology visit, subject to the model's history-based constraint.
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: EHR-derived clinical observations and medication/therapy timelines; activity and severity measures, medication history, anti-TNF exposure, and event times
legacy_cells.BD: Finite therapy-regimen category (six modeled therapies); no dose attributes stated
legacy_cells.BF: A therapy in the patient's medication history cannot be started again.
legacy_cells.BI: Unnamed (event-based controlled stochastic system with CTMC dynamics and MPC)
legacy_cells.BL: Irregular clinical-visit/medication events; CTMC transitions use the inter-event interval Δt; MPC prediction horizon N=4 events.
legacy_cells.BN: Monotonically non-decreasing historical severity; transition rates to lower-severity states fixed at zero; dynamics mode depends on therapy-start time, prior anti-TNF exposure, and current therapy.
legacy_cells.BS: Disease-activity/remission indicator derived from the state (yk = ak).
legacy_cells.BT: Activity/remission readout from the explicit disease state.
legacy_cells.BU: Minimize expected disease-activity cost over the horizon (inactive disease is rewarded), with terminal weight Δtterm=3 months and therapy-switch penalty rswitch=0.15.
legacy_cells.BV: Maximum-likelihood estimation of CTMC transition-rate matrices from interval-censored trajectories using EM; induction response parameters fitted by interval likelihood.
legacy_cells.CD: MPC horizon N=4 events; simulated follow-up extended up to 24 months.
legacy_cells.CG: 10 closed-loop MPC trajectories per patient for 10 sampled patients.
legacy_cells.CK: Minimize expected time in active disease over the horizon, with terminal cost, a therapy-switch penalty, and a constraint against restarting a therapy in the medication history.
legacy_cells.EC: In closed-loop simulation, observed-course cost was above or within the range of MPC costs for all 10 patients; for 4/10 patients, more than half of MPC runs had cost at or below observed care.
legacy_cells.ED: Compared simulated closed-loop MPC costs with each patient's observed EHR course: observed cost was above or within the MPC-cost range for all 10 sampled patients.
legacy_cells.EL: The induction time-constant confidence interval was wide and on the order of the observation cadence.
legacy_cells.FL: EHR-derived state and medication timeline → explicit state (therapy elapsed time, activity, historical severity, anti-TNF exposure, medication history) → mode-dependent CTMC dynamics → disease-activity output/cost → receding-horizon MPC over therapy regimens.
legacy_cells.FM: Proposes an event-based controlled stochastic model for chronic disease response; estimates treatment- and state-dependent CTMC dynamics from EHR trajectories with EM; formulates therapy selection as event-based MPC; demonstrates it for ulcerative colitis.
legacy_cells.FN: Identified 24 transition-rate matrices for six therapies from 3,318 patients and 33,706 intervals. In closed-loop simulation on 10 patients, observed cost was within or above the MPC range in all cases; more than half of MPC runs matched or bettered observed cost for 4/10 patients.
legacy_cells.FO: The induction time-constant confidence interval was wide and on the order of the observation cadence; bootstrap intervals were used to assess mode identifiability, while MPC/simulation used nominal estimates.
legacy_cells.FP: Use bootstrap estimates of model uncertainty to construct a robust formulation and advance data-driven clinical decision-support tools.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify limited head-to-head and multi-step treatment-sequence evidence from RCTs; fixed-step decision models mismatch irregular visits, while multistate models are often descriptive rather than used for control.
legacy_cells.FR: The reported controller evaluation is closed-loop simulation on 10 sampled patients using the learned CTMC for both prediction and simulated dynamics; it does not establish prospective clinical benefit, external validity, or identified causal treatment effects.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer; M8 Planner; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Keep the learned patient/scene simulator separate from the planner objective; constrain candidate actions and report closed-loop decision quality alongside model fidelity.

limitations: All 8 physical PDF pages were read as extracted text (including p. 8 Fig. 2, Conclusion, and References). Rendered page images were directly inspected for page 5 (Table I: q0=1.02 [0.76, 2.12] yr^-1, q_inf=0.38 [0.32, 0.43] yr^-1, tau_ind=47.75 [12.60, 118.54] days), page 7 (Fig. 1: J_obs vs 10 closed-loop MPC costs for P1-P10), and page 8 (Fig. 2: observed vs 10 MPC therapy sequences for two sampled patients).

No held-out retrospective validation split is reported; the 24 CTMC rate matrices are fitted in-sample on 3,318 patients and closed-loop MPC is evaluated on 10 patients sampled from the same fitting cohort inside the fitted model.
The legacy row was read from the root workbook (read only). Saved API drafts for B097 were not opened.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. Automated repair review, no independent human review.
notes: The paper models ulcerative colitis response to therapy as a CTMC with state and input dependent rates (24 mode-specific matrices from 3,318 patients and 33,706 intervals, fitted by EM) and selects therapy by receding-horizon MPC over six therapies. In closed-loop simulation on 10 patients drawn from the fitting cohort, observed costs fell above or within the MPC range for all 10 and more than half of MPC costs were at or below observed for 4. Classified L4, core, with a retrospective model fit and in-model policy evaluation. Source points: no held-out validation, in-model evaluation, associational dynamics.
